One-line judgment: a claims adjuster is not someone who pays out to a form, but someone who checks the policy and the facts and the evidence within an authorized limit, decides to pay, deny or refer for investigation, and is responsible for the conclusion; O*NET defines the occupation as reviewing settled and pending claims to ensure that payment and settlement comply with company practices and procedures, conferring with legal counsel on claims requiring litigation, and possibly settling insurance claims directly.

Signals to keep exploring: you are willing to write the doubts out clearly and escalate them when the evidence is insufficient, and can communicate through the process when a customer is highly emotional; the O*NET work context shows that 100% use email and telephone conversations every day, 93% write letters and memos and make decisions every day, 68% consider precision or accuracy extremely important, 62% feel time pressure every day, 46% encounter conflict situations every day, and 44%
face unpleasant or angry or discourteous people more than weekly.

Conditions for pausing before a large investment: you have not yet handled a complete claim requiring evidence collection and a written conclusion, and you have not checked policy clauses and exclusions; most positions in this occupation require a bachelor's degree (the education distribution is bachelor's 56%, high school 13% and some college but no degree 12%), and decisions must be made and be reviewable under authorized limits and time pressure.

Education, qualifications and authorization must be checked separately: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone Four (considerable preparation), SVP range 7.0 to below 8.0; in claims work, the position's authorized limit, the company's approval authority, industry certification or licensing requirements, and the jurisdiction's regulation of loss adjusting and claims are four different things; the O*NET page for this occupation lists 1
apprenticeship opportunity and several industry certification directions, and certification and licence and company authorization cannot substitute for one another.

In one line: this is an occupation where whether the policy clauses were read correctly, whether the evidence is sufficient, whether the authorized limit was exceeded and whether the conclusion can be reviewed and re-paid matter more than negotiation technique; if you are willing to carry traceable responsibility for your claim conclusions, it is worth serious consideration.

The work of claims adjusters, examiners and investigators can be divided into three connected but distinct work dimensions. The first is checking and analysis: review claim forms and records to determine the scope of insurance liability, check police reports and medical records and bills and property damage material to determine the degree of liability, and analyse the investigation findings and report conclusions and recommendations. The second is judgment and handling: pay and process claims within the authorized limit, investigate and evaluate and settle claims, adjust reserves or recommend reserves, and refer suspicious claims for
investigation or review. The third is communication and records: interview or correspond with agents and claimants to correct errors or omissions, confer with lawyers on claims requiring litigation, enter payments and reserves and new cases into the system with concise but sufficient documentation, maintain claim files and take part in claims committees and mediation or hearings.
Check the policy and the evidence and determine the scope of liability

Receive the report and check the policy and endorsements and exclusions, collect police and medical and property and employment evidence, cross-check the consistency and timeline between statements and documents, judge under the clauses whether it falls within the cover and the liability proportion, write the conclusion and the basis and flag uncertain items, and decide under the authorized limit to pay or refer for review or investigation
Approve payments and reserves within the authorized limit

Calculate the payable amount under the clauses and documents, check elements such as the deductible and limits and depreciation and subrogation, make the decision within the authorized limit or submit it for higher approval, enter the payment and reserve and update the file, explain the conclusion and the basis and the appeal channel to the claimant, and report anomalies and excess cases under policy

Maintain claim files and settled records and the list awaiting analysis; refer suspicious claims to an investigator or adjuster; collect evidence for disputed claims; take part in mediation or hearings; and submit reports to the data processing department.

Common adjacent positions include insurance underwriters, real estate appraisers and assessors, compliance officers, fraud examiners and investigators and analysts, and compensation and benefits and job analysis specialists. On the boundaries: underwriters assess underwriting risk and decide whether to insure; appraisers assess the value of the subject matter; compliance officers monitor compliance with rules; this occupation approves the payment conclusion within the policy and the authorized limit.

Six recurring occupational judgments: whether the policy clauses and exclusions were read correctly; whether the evidence is sufficient to support the conclusion; whether the statements and documents are consistent; whether the payment amount and reserve are calculated correctly; whether suspicious and anomalous cases are referred under policy; and whether the conclusion is within the authorized limit and reviewable.
Judgment one: whether the clauses and exclusions were read correctly

Editorial check suggestion: check the applicability and validity of the policy, endorsements, special agreements and exclusions clause by clause. Article 17 of China's Insurance Law requires the insurer to highlight and clearly explain exemption clauses, and Article 30 provides interpretation rules for disputed clauses; a denial cannot be issued automatically just because exclusion wording is present. Doubts are submitted to legal and compliance for checking, and internal consultation does not automatically extend the statutory time limit.
Judgment two: whether the evidence is sufficient to support the conclusion

Editorial advice is to list separately the lawfully obtained evidence that supports and does not support the conclusion, noting the source, time and gaps. Articles 22—25 of China's Insurance Law require a single timely notice requesting further evidence, timely assessment and payment or refusal notification within the statutory period, and internal investigation or referral is not a reason for unlimited delay.
Judgment three: whether the statements and documents are consistent

Compare the times and parts and amounts in the reported statement against the medical or repair or police records, record the verification process and conclusion for inconsistencies, and refer suspicious signs under policy.
Judgment four: whether the payment amount and reserve are calculated correctly

Editorial check suggestion: check the deductible, limits, depreciation, subrogation and prior payments under the applicable clauses, keeping the values taken and the process; reserves are checked under the method and authority actually approved by the company, and trial calculations or the checklist on this page are not treated as authority to adjust them.
Judgment five: whether suspicious and anomalous cases are referred under policy
Report and refer excess and anomalous and suspected fraud cases under policy, and do not handle matters beyond your authority or expertise yourself.
Judgment six: whether the conclusion is within the authorized limit

Confirm your own authorized limit and the types of case you may decide independently; claims beyond the limit or involving litigation and liability disputes are submitted to a superior or legal position with a record of the approval.

Claims adjusters, examiners and investigators review settled and pending claims to confirm that payment and settlement comply with company practices and procedures, confer with legal counsel on claims requiring litigation, and may settle insurance claims directly; the typical closed loop is checking the policy and report materials, collecting and analysing evidence, approving payment or denial within the authorized limit, recording the reasons and handling review and appeals.

paragraphs: The six directions share some capabilities with this occupation: reading rules and clauses, collecting and checking evidence, written records, and communication with the other party. The real differences lie in the object of judgment (underwriting risk, or liability for loss; value, or financial records), the point in time (before underwriting, or after an incident) and the authority (claim approval limit, or compliance or audit authority). When choosing, it is better to test with one deliverable evidence check and claim conclusion than to compare titles.

The basis for comparison is the task and work activity descriptions on the O*NET-SOC 13-1031.00 page, the adjacent occupation notes registered in this evidence route, and the public occupational materials for each adjacent occupation; the comparison is an editorial compilation and does not constitute a conclusion about scope of practice or exchange of qualifications.

The table below compares positions and occupations adjacent to this occupation: insurance underwriters, real estate appraisers and assessors, compliance officers, fraud examiners and investigators and analysts, compensation and benefits and job analysis specialists, and accountants and auditors. The four columns each answer the same kind of question: what this direction does, where the key difference from this occupation lies, and what kind of person is better suited to choosing it.

Insurance underwriters assess underwriting risk and decide whether to insure and at what rate; this occupation approves the payment conclusion after the cover is in force, and the two differ in the object of judgment and the point in time.

People willing to assess risk and price before underwriting are suited to the underwriting direction; people willing to check evidence and approve payment after an incident are suited to this occupation.
Assess the risk of the insured subject matter and decide the underwriting conditions and rate, with outputs mainly underwriting decisions and risk records.
Insurance underwriters
Real estate appraisers and assessors assess real estate value for transactions and mortgages and expropriation; this occupation approves the amount of loss within the scope of insurance liability.
People willing to do real estate valuation and market analysis are suited to the appraisal direction; people willing to determine insurance liability and loss are suited to this occupation.
Assess real estate value and issue appraisal reports, with outputs mainly appraisal reports and market analysis.
Real estate appraisers and assessors

Compliance officers monitor whether the institution and the business comply with the rules and organize compliance training and inspections; this occupation handles the application of clauses and the conclusion in individual claims.
People willing to do rule interpretation and compliance checking are suited to the compliance direction; people willing to make case judgments and communicate are suited to this occupation.
Establish and carry out compliance policies and inspections, with outputs mainly compliance opinions and inspection and training records.
Compliance officers

Fraud examiners and investigators focus on identifying and investigating fraud patterns and support law enforcement and internal investigations; this occupation handles routine claims and refers suspicious cases under policy once identified.
People willing to analyse fraud patterns and investigate are suited to the fraud investigation direction; people willing to do routine claim approval and communication are suited to this occupation.
Analyse suspicious patterns and carry out investigation and evidence gathering, with outputs mainly investigation reports and lead analysis.
Fraud examiners and investigators

Compensation and benefits and job analysis specialists are responsible for job evaluation and pay structures and benefit plans; this occupation handles insurance claims rather than human resources compensation matters.
People willing to do job and pay analysis are suited to the compensation and benefits direction; people willing to make claim judgments are suited to this occupation.
Carry out job evaluation and pay and benefit data analysis, with outputs mainly pay plans and analysis reports.
Compensation and benefits and job analysis specialists

Accountants and auditors are responsible for financial records and statements and audit; the object of judgment in this occupation is insurance liability and loss evidence, and both require awareness of evidence and standards but the applicable rules differ.
People willing to do financial accounting and audit are suited to the accounting and audit direction; people willing to judge claim evidence and clauses are suited to this occupation.
Maintain financial records and carry out audit and assurance, with outputs mainly financial statements and audit opinions.
Accountants and auditors

Moving from this occupation to an adjacent direction usually requires filling in new knowledge and evidence: the underwriting direction requires risk and pricing knowledge, the appraisal direction requires valuation methods and a practice pathway, the compliance direction requires a rule system and inspection experience, the fraud investigation direction requires evidence gathering and analysis training, and the accounting and audit direction requires accounting standards and an audit pathway. Clause reading and evidence checking transfer, but the authorization and standards system of each direction must be obtained anew.

entries.answer: Day-to-day work centres on checking policy terms, analysing evidence, communicating and recording: reviewing claim forms and records to determine coverage, re-checking police, medical and property materials to establish the degree of liability, paying and processing claims and adjusting reserves within delegated authority, communicating with claimants and agents and lawyers, and entering cases into systems and maintaining files, attending mediation or court hearings when necessary. The O*NET Work Context fields show that 100% use email and telephone conversation every day, 93% write letters and memos every day and 62% feel time pressure every day.
entries.question: What do claims adjusters, examiners and investigators do every day?

entries.answer: Underwriters assess underwriting risk and decide whether to accept a risk; appraisers value real estate; compliance officers monitor conformity with rules; fraud examiners and investigators focus on fraud patterns and investigations; this occupation determines the payout conclusion within delegated authority after cover is in force. Shared skills do not mean the roles are interchangeable: the object of judgement, the point in time and the authority system differ.
entries.question: Where is the boundary between this occupation and adjacent ones?

entries.answer: That cannot be inferred. The core tasks of this occupation include applying policy terms and judging exclusions, verifying evidence and identifying suspicious claims, and being accountable for the claims conclusions signed by the individual and the organisation; AI output can neither replace delegated authority nor remove the duty to record faithfully and escalate under the institution's rules.
entries.question: Will AI replace claims adjusters, examiners and investigators?

entries.answer: The earlier-affected stages are those that can be entered in structured form: document extraction and field entry, amount calculation and quote comparison, drafts of correspondence and records, and compiling lists and files. The later-affected stages are those requiring professional judgement and accountability: applying policy terms and exclusions, identifying and escalating suspicious claims, and handling disputed and litigated cases.
entries.question: Which tasks are most easily automated?

entries.answer: Reading policy terms and exclusions, judging whether evidence is sufficient, spotting inconsistencies in interviews and on site, and reaching conclusions within delegated authority that can be reviewed and re-paid. These skills depend on professional training and institutional constraints.

Certifications, licences and a company's delegated claims authority serve different purposes, and delegated claims authority is set by institutional rules and rises step by step.
